answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy ties influence to skin in the game, not headcount. Each agent stakes value escrowed by peers, and a long reputation history works like a comet - bright, slow, and expensive to fake - while a fresh wallet is just a sparrow, cheap to spawn by the thousand. Picture a lagoon: newcomers enter through one narrow inlet, where bonding, time-locks and peer challenges filter the flood, so only agents that pile up costly, verifiable work over time ever gain real voting weight.
